newsitem.title: USA: Ryder CEO backs 1997 estimates of $2.20-$2.25.
newsitem.headline: Ryder CEO backs 1997 estimates of $2.20-$2.25.

text.p: Ryder System Inc Chief Executive Anthony Burns on Friday said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates that the company would earn $2.20 to $2.25 a share in 1997.
"We continue to be comfortable with the Street estimates," he told reporters after the company's annual meeting. "...$2.20 to $2.25, we're comfortable with that."
Burns said he expected capital spending in 1997 to be less than last year's $1.3 billion. In 1995, the transportation company's capital spending was $2.2 billion.

For 1996, Ryder posted a net loss of $41.3 million, or $0.51 per share, including an after-tax extraordinary loss on the retirement of debt of $10 million, or $0.12 per common share, and restructuring and other charges of $164 million, or $2.02 per share.
Burns repeated that the company expected to make an announcement about the disposition of its auto-carrier unit during the second quarter.

During the meeting, the company announced that 34.7 million shares had voted in favor of a shareholder proposal calling for the annual election of Ryder's directors. Though the measure failed -- it needed 38.6 million votes to pass -- Burns acknowledged the large number of shares that favored the proposal and said the board would discuss the issue at its next meeting.
